checks.name: STRESS.topstep.returns.note
checks.detail: '`pnl_under_account_constraints` is what the ACCOUNT realised - the daily limit applied and the path stopped at liquidation. The other three are strategy-level and ignore the account entirely.'

checks.name: attrition.bars_in_window
checks.detail: canonical 100450 vs legacy 100059: The two paths COUNT at different points, they do not keep different bars. `futures_discover.load` applies the window and the one-contract-per-session filter in one function and returns the result, so its bar count is already net of the multi-contract day. The canonical path counts the window first and the contract filter second, so its count still includes that day. The difference is exactly the bars of the dropped session(s) and the KEPT sessions are identical.

checks.name: attrition.sessions_in_window
checks.detail: canonical 261 vs legacy 260: Same mechanism as bars_in_window: the canonical count is taken before the multi-contract filter and the legacy count after it.

checks.name: attrition.sessions_dropped_multi_contract
checks.detail: canonical 1 vs legacy -1: The legacy path reports -1 (unknown) because `fd.load` has already discarded those days by the time it returns; the count is not recoverable without re-reading the file. Stated as unknown rather than guessed at.

checks.name: provenance
checks.detail: canonical declares CONTINUOUS_UNADJUSTED / manifest e0f411ac6298e690 / frame 33275bc8f5bf9148; legacy declares nothing. The canonical path declares the data form, the roll method, the adjustment method, the manifest id, the frame fingerprint and the quality status. The legacy path declares none of them - it has nowhere to put them. That asymmetry IS the reason for the migration and is not a discrepancy in the result.

checks.name: gates_run
checks.detail: canonical ['schema.validate_frame', 'data.quality.check', 'futures_cme.dataquality.require_usable'] vs legacy ['futures_cme.dataquality.require_usable']. The canonical path runs three gates (canonical schema, canonical quality, futures validator); the legacy path runs one (the futures validator). The canonical path is strictly stronger - it runs every check the legacy path runs, and more.

checks.name: wall_clock
checks.detail: canonical 24.6s vs legacy 9.2s. The canonical path is slower because it runs the schema validation and the full quality gate on every load. That is a cost, not a difference in the answer.

canonical_provenance.describe: FEATURE DATA and EXECUTION DATA are the SAME series: ibkr-MNQ-1min [CONTINUOUS_UNADJUSTED] manifest e0f411ac6298e690 frame 33275bc8f5bf9148

legacy_provenance.describe: LEGACY PATH: bars read straight from the provider file. No data form, no roll method, no adjustment method, no manifest id and no frame fingerprint were declared, because this path has nowhere to put them.
